findings.title: removeStoredCredentialById does not remove federated recovery codes
findings.body: The credential may now reside in user storage (retrieved via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential which checks federated storage first). removeStoredCredentialById operates only on local stored credentials and will not remove a federated credential, leaving the exhausted credential in user storage. Subsequently, the required action is added, causing duplicate credentials when the user reconfigures. A federated-specific removal method or clearing the credential via updateCredential should be used.

findings.title: getCredentials loses used state for recovery codes
findings.body: The getCredentials method deserializes raw codes and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...), which creates a model with all codes marked unused. Any usage tracking from the provider (if implemented) would be lost, causing RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential to always return a model where allCodesUsed() is false. This prevents the authenticator from detecting exhausted codes and triggering reconfiguration. Additionally, the provider's isValid does not track usage, so codes can be reused indefinitely. The creation path in CredentialHelper only passes raw codes to user storage, not the hashed/stateful model, making it impossible for providers to track used state correctly.

findings.title: Recovery codes cannot be disabled or removed via admin API
findings.body: disableCredentialType only handles OTP types; recovery codes are ignored. Additionally, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream (line 254) does not include recovery codes, so they won't be listed. This means administrators or account management cannot remove recovery codes from federated users, leaving stale credentials and preventing proper lifecycle management. These methods should be extended to support RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE.

findings.title: Optional.get() can throw if no recovery credential
findings.body: credentialModelOpt.get() will throw NoSuchElementException if RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential returns empty. While this bean is likely only used when a credential exists, relying on that implicit precondition is fragile; a missing credential would cause a server error instead of a graceful handling.

findings.title: Non-deterministic selection of federated recovery credential
findings.body: getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst() returns the first credential from an unordered stream. If multiple federated providers provide recovery codes, the selected credential may vary, leading to inconsistent behavior in checking allCodesUsed or retrieving the next code. A deterministic ordering or a check across all credentials should be considered.
